notes: 107 of 328 external reads return real sine data (0x0096ca93, 0x012d9456, ... at 0x0800bb5c onward), so the table is present and read. The output is still a monotone ramp (49-61 distinct sample values per block) with no oscillator term

hypothesis: Passing the real note to onNoteOn makes the factory engines track pitch
test: Call onNoteOn(0, note, ctx) with notes 45/57/69/81 instead of a fixed 69, and measure the spectral peak
notes: digital peaks at 753.1/745.7/753.1/753.1 Hz for requests of 110/220/440/880 Hz - a fixed 48 kHz/64 block rate. chord gives 326.5/166.0/1314.8/96.0 Hz, no consistent ratio. The one earlier harness bug (hardcoded note 69) was real but fixing it changes nothing

hypothesis: The factory engines ignore the pitch argument entirely
test: Log every sine-table read address inside digital's render and take the per-sample stride, at 110 Hz and 440 Hz
notes: The stride IS the requested frequency in bytes per sample: offsets advance 0,108,220,328,440 at 110 Hz (deltas 108/112 alternating) and 0,440,880,1320 at 440 Hz. The oscillator index therefore advances proportionally to pitch, so pitch does reach the oscillator

hypothesis: The oscillator term reaches the output buffer
test: Measure energy at the predicted oscillator frequency (f * 48000 / 0x8000) in both the whole render and the steady-state tail
notes: That frequency carries only 0.02-0.33 of the peak energy while a 753 Hz block-rate staircase dominates every render; in the steady-state tail digital peaks at 53.5 Hz regardless of pitch. The oscillator runs but its contribution never reaches the output at audible level

hypothesis: digital's output is the sine table lookup, oscillating each sample
test: Watch both output store sites (0x81be64a2 left, 0x81be64b6 right) with registers and the two most recent sine-table taps, on the sixth block of a 440 Hz render
notes: The stored sample is R4 (left) and R6 (right), and no sine-table read occurs at all in that block - the read count that varies with pitch comes from the early blocks only. Steady-state output is a ramp through R4/R6 while R7 carries a large accumulator-like value that is never converted to a sample

hypothesis: digital's oscillator uses its in-module 16-bit band entries at 0x81be69d4
test: Log every read inside 0x81be6900-0x81be6a80 across eight render blocks and compare the address sets and counts per block
notes: Exactly 12 reads per block, of the same 9 distinct addresses (0x81be69f8, 0x81be6a04, 0x81be6a0c, ...) from the fixed sites 0x81be61e8/0x81be61ea/0x81be61f4, identical in every block: that is the band-selection table read once per block. Nothing is read at the 16-bit band entries 0x81be69d4, so they are not the oscillator

hypothesis: The sine lookup stops firing in later blocks
test: Count sine-table reads per block with the window widened to 0x0800a000-0x08020000, over ten blocks
notes: The lookup never stops: every block performs 130 reads (about two per output sample) and the pointer advances 440 bytes per read, marching from 0x0800bb44 to 0x08013xxx. The earlier 'reads stop in later blocks' reading was an artefact of a counting window that ended at 0x0800d400

hypothesis: Removing the per-block DC reveals the oscillator as a clean tone
test: Subtract each 64-frame block's mean before taking the spectrum, with the pitch scaled so the oscillator targets 220/440/880 Hz
notes: The peak stays at 751.1 Hz for all three targets - the ramp's intra-block slope steps repeat at the 64-sample block rate and dominate the spectrum even after per-block DC removal

hypothesis: The pitch argument is a byte stride into a quarter-sine table of 8191 words, so output = input * 48000/32768
test: Pass q = 300/440/600 Hz and measure energy at 440, 644.5 and 880 Hz. The model predicts 440, 644 and 880 respectively
notes: q=300 peaks at 440 Hz (2.21e-3 vs 3.7e-4 at 644) and q=440 peaks at 644 Hz (1.26e-3 vs 3.4e-4 at 440), exactly as predicted by stride/32768*48000. The third probe (q=600, expected 880) instead peaks at 440, so the model holds over at least two bands but not all

hypothesis: The shared L2 table at 0x0800bb48 is a full sine table
test: Read the segment's 8191 words and count sign changes and extremes
notes: All 2000 sampled words are positive and monotone from 1,647,049 to 2,145,962,988 (0.999 of full scale) with zero sign changes, i.e. a quarter-sine over 8191 words, not a full waveform

hypothesis: The factory engines can play correct notes with the pitch argument scaled by 32768/48000
test: Pass pitch = f * 0.6827 to each factory engine and test whether energy at f beats its 0.75x and 1.5x neighbours, at 220 and 440 Hz
notes: digital plays both notes through the app path (energy 6.2e-3 and 5.0e-3 against neighbour maxima of 2.7e-3 and 9.9e-4 in the direct harness, and 1.0e+5 vs 9.0e+4 at 440 Hz through render_clip), and 7 of 8 probed pitches (110/220/330/440/550/660/880) beat their neighbours. chord, cluster, electric, ep, organ, sampleplayergain, synthsampler and volt do not

hypothesis: organ and cluster are silent because state+0x10 is zero
test: Log the state/params/amp reads that precede their early exit, then seed state+0x10 with 1..6, 0xff and 0x100
notes: Both exit after 19 and 21 steps having read only state+0x10 == 0, so that read is the gate; but seeding it across eight values leaves organ at peak 0.0000 and cluster at a constant 2e-4 regardless of the seed, so state+0x10 is a necessary condition rather than the missing input

hypothesis: The silent engines' state+0x10 gate is a level that must be seeded with the pitch argument
test: Decompile organ's render to read the branch, then seed state+0x10 (and +0x14/+0x18/+0x1c) with the pitch, 0x40000000, 0x7fffffff and 0x08000000 on organ, cluster and electric
notes: organ's decompile shows 'if (*(int *)(param_4 + 0x10) == 0) return;' followed by a write of param_2 into it, so the seed is right in principle; but no seed makes organ audible (peak stays 0.0000), cluster stays at a constant 2e-4, and electric reaches peak 0.0315 with 0x40000000 while still not tracking pitch at 220 or 440 Hz

hypothesis: The four erroring engines fail because their calls land outside the mapped module
test: Map the OS image alongside the engine (via opzos.build) so out-of-window calls resolve into firmware code, then render
notes: With the OS mapped the calls do resolve - analoga, saw013a and ministringshort proceed past the previous 'keeps calling outside its window' error and instead raise 'call did not return', and fm003b never returns at all (over 1400 s). So those engines genuinely want the OS to service them, which is a sharper statement than the old error

hypothesis: electric can be calibrated into a working engine by seeding state+0x10
test: Sweep the value seeded in state+0x10..0x1c over 150-600 Hz and measure energy at 440 Hz
notes: Energy at 440 responds only weakly (2.6e-4 to 4.3e-4) and never beats its 330/660 Hz neighbours at any seed, while the pitch argument has no effect at all on its output

hypothesis: The silent engines need the amp object's byte fields (amp+0x14/+0x15) that the OS writes at note start
test: Seed the whole word at amp+0x14 with 0x01, 0x02 and 0xff on organ, cluster, sampleplayergain and synthsampler, together with the pitch seeded in state+0x10..0x1c
notes: No seed changes anything: organ and sampleplayergain and synthsampler stay at peak 0.0000 and cluster at a constant 2e-4. Separately, organ with params at 0x7fffffff does progress, but then raises 'keeps calling outside its window', i.e. it needs the OS once it gets that far

hypothesis: Stubbing the host-services table unblocks the engines that call outside their window
test: Point all 13 host-table dwords at an RTS stub inside the machine window, then render organ, analoga, saw013a and ministringshort
notes: All four still raise 'keeps calling outside its window', so the offending calls do not go through the table entries. Reading opzsim's emulation explains it: an out-of-window call already returns 0 to the engine, and the engine keeps calling - raising the consecutive-call limit to 200,000 (new HOST_CALL_LIMIT constant) does not let any of them finish, so they spin on a host call that returns 0

hypothesis: Executing the real OS routine organ waits on (0x800314c0) unblocks it
test: Identify the call target by logging out-of-window calls, then implement ProgCtrl opc 0xD/0xE (CLI/STI) which the routine hit, and re-run organ with the OS image mapped
notes: The fix is real - 0x800314c0 now executes and returns in 38 steps with R0=0 - but organ then runs to 0x80000003 and executes garbage (0x7980), i.e. a call through OS data that is zero in an unbooted image. analoga, saw013a and ministringshort still 'call did not return'

hypothesis: The looping engines wait on a host call whose return value is a buffer pointer
test: Make the out-of-window return value configurable (new machine attribute host_return) and run organ, analoga, saw013a and ministringshort with 0, 0x81b00000 and 0x81500000
notes: All twelve combinations still raise 'keeps calling outside its window', so the loops do not depend on the returned pointer - the engines are waiting on OS state that a single return value cannot supply

hypothesis: The looping engines are waiting on an OS response inside their loop
test: Disassemble organ's loop at 0x81b7d5b0-0x81b7d630 with Ghidra DumpBytes
notes: The loop is not a host wait: LSETUP(0x81b7d5c0) with a CALL to organ's own 0x81b7ed08 using R1=0x64 (100) as divisor, then P1 = 0x81b7f698 + (result << 2) and R0 = [P1] at 0x81b7d5dc. The 'outside its window' reads are that table lookup, so the index comes back negative and runs off the front of the module's table

hypothesis: organ's negative table index comes from a pitch below its band base
test: Log the divide's operands at 0x81b7d5c6/0x81b7d5ca, read the band table at 0x81b7f6cc-0x81b7f6e0, then try pitches from 0x012c0000 to 0x186a00000
notes: The numerator is a phase-derived small negative (-18, -19) while the divisor is 100, and the routine saturates to 0x31eb851 for any negative input, so the table index runs off the module. The band table is an octave ladder in Q16 Hz (24.3, 48.6, 97.2 ... 777.6) but every pitch from 300 Hz to 1.6 MHz still fails, so the pitch value is not what drives the numerator negative

hypothesis: The three working factory engines can also be played live through opzplay
test: Extend the JIT to pass six stack arguments (factory engines need context, params and amp) and to handle the sop=3 shift variant, then point opzplay at engines-official/digital.engine
notes: Both JIT extensions are in and our own engines still play (29 us per block, realtime), but factory engines stop at further gaps: Dsp32Shf (register shift, sigd=0xC) is not emitted and one form decodes as Dsp32Mac (sig2=0), which the interpreter does not implement either. opzplay therefore raises Unsupported for every factory engine, which is an honest failure rather than wrong pitch

hypothesis: Closing the JIT's NOP32 and Dsp32Shf gaps lets factory engines run in the realtime player
test: Add the NOP32 test and Dsp32Shf (register shift) to opzjit, then point opzplay at digital, ep and chord
notes: Both fixes are correct and our engines are unaffected (29.7 us per block, 440.1 Hz), but the factory modules then stop on instruction 0xe0a2 - LSETUP in its register-count form, which opzjit does not implement in any form. Our own engines are loop-free, which is why this never surfaced

hypothesis: The four erroring engines fail on a pitch-dependent index, as organ's loop does
test: Render analoga, saw013a, ministringshort and fm003b at pitch arguments from 50 Hz to 1200 Hz with the pitch also seeded in state+0x10..0x1c
notes: All twenty-four runs raise the same 'keeps calling outside its window' error at every pitch, so these four are structurally blocked rather than mistuned - unlike digital, whose calibration sweep found a working factor

hypothesis: A blanket fill of the silent engines' state block unlocks them
test: Fill all 128 state words with 0x01010101, 0x08080808, 0x00010001 and 0x00FF00FF on organ, cluster, sampleplayergain, synthsampler and electric
notes: organ, cluster, synthsampler stay at peak 0.0000 and sampleplayergain raises; electric reaches a constant peak of 0.0181 at every fill, and a single-note neighbour test then passes at 330 and 660 Hz purely because its fixed spectrum has energy there. Requiring two notes, as opzfactorycheck does, correctly rejects it

hypothesis: chord and ep play as robustly as digital across the range
test: Render all three at 110/165/220/330/440/659 Hz through render_clip and test energy at each target against its 0.75x and 1.5x neighbours
notes: digital passes 5 of 6 (fails only 659); chord and ep pass only 220 and 440 and fail at exactly the 0.75x and 1.5x neighbours, i.e. on their own interval components. A chord engine's spectrum legitimately contains a fifth, so the two-note result overstates them: only digital is robust across the range

hypothesis: A band-limited FFT peak, after removing the block ramp, settles whether chord, digital and ep track
test: Moving-average high-pass (64 samples), Hann window, rFFT over 60-2000 Hz, peak/f0 at 110/220/330/440/659 Hz
notes: Results are self-contradictory: chord reads 2.03/2.04/2.04 (a clean octave) at 330/440/659 Hz but 6.29 at 110 Hz, digital runs 6.82 down to 1.14, ep 8.36 down to 1.40. First-difference high-passing instead pushed the peaks to Nyquist. These engines' output carries non-musical energy that survives every simple filter, so peak-based analysis cannot decide tracking for them

hypothesis: Implementing LSETUP in the JIT is what keeps the factory engines out of the live player
test: Add LSETUP (immediate and register-count forms) with static back-edges, plus the Dsp32Shf families popcount, extract and signbits, then run opzplay on digital
notes: All four are implemented and our own engines still play (52 us per block, 17/17 pitch tests), but the chain continues: digital next stops on ALU2op opc=0x8, DIVQ - the conditional division step that opzsim does not implement either, since its interpreter path never reaches it

hypothesis: The JIT can be brought up to factory engines one instruction class at a time
test: Implement LSETUP, Dsp32Shf popcount/extract/signbits/ExpAdj and ALU2op DIVQ/DIVS in opzjit from the Ghidra SLEIGH sources, then run opzplay on digital
notes: Each class is now implemented and correct - the interpreter already had DIVQ/DIVS, and the JIT's versions follow instr16/12-ALU2op.sinc exactly - and our own engines still play (51.8 us per block, 17/17). The chain then reaches Dsp32Alu aopc=0x19, AddSubAC0, which reads the ASTAT AC0 bit that opzjit does not model at all; a partial implementation would silently diverge from the interpreter

hypothesis: With LSETUP, the shift families, DIVQ/DIVS and AddSubAC0 in the JIT, digital plays live
test: Run opzplay on engines-official/digital.engine after implementing those classes and modelling ASTAT AQ/AC0
notes: The classes are correct - and the engine's own code runs at 7 us per block in isolation - but with the host-services table populated the JIT path calls an OS routine and never returns, so the ctypes call spins in C. opzplay now refuses factory engines with a clear message rather than hanging the audio thread; they remain auditionable through opzenginetool

hypothesis: A step budget plus a routed loop-check is enough to make factory engines play under the JIT
test: Add opz_call's 4,000,000-step cap (reporting OPZ_STUCK), route every case exit through the loop check so a taken branch cannot skip it, and drive digital through the player
notes: The engine no longer hangs - it hits the cap and returns -2, and the player renders 40 blocks of peak 0.0000. So it is genuinely looping inside the JIT path under the full player sequence, not in isolation, and the loop logic still disagrees with opzsim. opzplay refuses factory engines again with that reason rather than playing silence

hypothesis: The JIT's factory-engine loop comes from a bad loop count on a path the interpreter also takes
test: Expose LC/LB/LE from the generated code and read them after the stuck call, then log opzsim's loop frames for the same address
notes: The JIT is stuck in a loop ending at 0x81be6898 with LC=-800046 (0xfff3c992) - a negative count, so it would iterate about 4 billion times. The interpreter never registers any loop ending at that address at all, so the two take different control flow well before it: this is a decode or arithmetic divergence inside the JIT, not a shared loop bug

hypothesis: The JIT loop can be reproduced from a minimal harness, so it can be bisected
test: Add a pc trace and step budget to opz_call, then drive digital's render from a hand-built harness with the same table, params, amp object, note-on sequence and frequency the player uses
notes: Every hand-built variant returns normally (18 traced instructions, repeated blocks fine, note-on with and without note-off first), while the same engine through opzplay's Engine object returns -2 with OPZ_STUCK=0x81be6890. The divergence therefore depends on some remaining difference in the player's setup, so it cannot yet be bisected from a minimal case

hypothesis: The JIT's player-path loop is caused by engine state differences
test: Dump the player's and a minimal harness's engine memory just before render and diff them word by word, then build the same source under two cache names
notes: The two memory images are byte-identical (0 differing words of 528384) and the arguments match, yet one build returns -2 and the other runs normally; the same source compiled under two names produces dylibs of different size (50704 vs 50712 bytes) with divergent behaviour. That is undefined behaviour in the generated C - the goto-based loop check jumping into scope - so the emission needs redesigning rather than debugging further

hypothesis: Moving the loop back-edge into the dispatch loop fixes the JIT's factory-engine hang
test: Replace the per-case goto-based check with a post-instruction check at the top of the dispatch loop (matching opzsim's _loop_end), then drive digital through the player
notes: The undefined behaviour is gone - the check no longer jumps into a case's scope, and our own engines are unaffected (56.8 us per block, 17/17, sweep unchanged at 2 detuned / 3 flat / 3 loops / 5 needs-state / 8 silent) - but the player path still returns -2: the engine's LC is about 4.29e9 there. Combined with the interpreter never registering a loop at that address, the JIT takes a different control path, so a decode/flow divergence remains beyond the loop mechanics

hypothesis: The device project files (.opz) carry the runtime plug state the engines need
test: Read the ten project files: size, embedded address patterns, and whether they contain 'engines/' or plug configuration strings
notes: Each .opz is 342,848 bytes of pattern and sample data - only 48 dwords in the whole file look like OS addresses (4 L2, 1 L1) and there is no 'engines/' or 'plugs' string anywhere - so they are song data, not a snapshot of the plug registry the engines consult

hypothesis: The audible-but-untuned engines need a different voice gain to track pitch
test: Sweep amp+0x04 over 0x10000000, 0x40000000, 0x60000000 and 0x7fffffff on cluster, electric, volt, sampleplayergain and synthsampler, testing 220 and 440 Hz against their neighbours
notes: None of the twenty engine/gain combinations makes any of the five track: every one either stays silent, stays fixed-spectrum, or fails the neighbour test at both notes. The gain is not the missing parameter

hypothesis: The silent engines need the OS's five-argument init framing (state, voice, 0x0800bb44, 0x8156f2b8, ...)
test: Call init with those five arguments both in registers and on the stack for organ, cluster, sampleplayergain, synthsampler and electric, then render 440 Hz
notes: Output is byte-identical to the two-argument call: organ, sampleplayergain and synthsampler stay at peak 0.0000, electric at 0.0155 and cluster at 2e-4 (its known fixed spectrum). Only chord had been tested with this framing before, and it too was unchanged

hypothesis: The eight factory effect engines were never tested
test: Feed a 440 Hz sine to each factory effect through renderFX with the five-argument stack the sweep uses, plus host memory, and measure peak/rms
notes: First time these were exercised: crush (peak 0.019, rms 1.7e-2) and chorus2 (peak 0.027, rms 2.5e-2) transform the input rather than passing it through, while chorus and dist are silent, reverb raises 'keeps calling outside its window' and delay, tapetwo and fdnreverb never return. Neither working effect is demonstrably correct - chorus2 holds a constant 0x36af009 - so this establishes they run, not that they behave

hypothesis: The silent factory effects (chorus, dist) need their state block seeded, as the instruments do
test: Seed fx_state with 0x7fffffff, 0x40000000 and 0x01010101 across 0x100 bytes and feed a 440 Hz sine, comparing distinct outputs and peak
notes: Both stay at peak 0.0000 with a single distinct output under every seed, while the same harness makes crush produce 195 distinct outputs and chorus2 308 from a ramp. So the seeding that helps instruments does not reach these two effects at all

hypothesis: dist is silent because it dereferences unmapped OS data (host-table entry 0x81128264)
test: Decompile dist's renderFX to read its guard, seed its state fields with in/out/length in every order, then map the whole OS image so 0x81128264 resolves
notes: The decompile shows 'iVar9 = *(int *)(*(int *)(DAT_81bfa4f8 + 8) + uVar8 * 4)', i.e. it indexes through the host table's third dword, and it writes through module pointers DAT_81bfa554/558. Mapping all 164 OS segments makes 0x81128264 readable, and no state layout produces output: dist stays at peak 0.0000 with a single distinct value

hypothesis: crush and chorus2 can be verified correct by their transfer function, as our own effects were
test: Feed known constants (0x10000000 through 0x40000001) through crush and chorus2 with two settling passes and read the steady output
notes: Neither has a clean transfer function: a one-bit input change moves crush's output from 0x012d53ca to 0x0259f50a, and chorus2 integrates slowly (0x031adf4f to 0x031eec10 across the whole range). Both are state-dependent processors, consistent with crush's own parameter names resample/vector and chorus2 being a modulated delay, so 'correct' cannot be established from the mapping alone

hypothesis: delay, tapetwo and fdnreverb never return
test: Raise the call budget from 200,000 to 3,000,000 steps and call init, then renderFX, for each of the three
notes: Their init does return: fdnreverb in 62,408 steps, delay in 524,333 and tapetwo in 524,606 - the earlier 'never returns' was a step limit that was too low, not a hang. After init, delay renders peak 0.0000 and tapetwo hits a null function pointer, so they still produce no audio

hypothesis: delay renders silence because its init's buffer allocation is missing
test: Raise the step budget so init completes, then inspect the LSETUP at 0x81be4cf8 and where the cleared pointer comes from
notes: delay's init runs LSETUP(0x81be4d06) with P0=0x00000000 as destination and P1=0x00100000 (1 MB) as size, so it clears address 0 upwards and stores nothing: ctx and every module global read back zero afterwards. Its renderFX then reads state+0x00/+0x04/+0x0c, all zero, and writes silence. The buffer pointer is host-supplied, which is the same wall as the instruments

hypothesis: delay's buffer pointer is a stack argument, and providing one makes it render
test: Pass a scratch buffer as init's third/fourth register argument and as four stack words, then renderFX, counting how much of the buffer init touches
notes: Passing it on the stack does reach the engine - init leaves 49 of 256 words in that buffer nonzero, against 8 with no buffer - so the buffer is a stack argument rather than a register one. renderFX is still silent (peak 0.0000, one distinct value) and tapetwo still raises a null function pointer, so receiving a buffer is necessary but not sufficient

hypothesis: The silent effects fail because init and renderFX were given different state objects
test: Call init and renderFX with the same state object, once using ctx and once an fx_state block, with a buffer on the stack, for delay, tapetwo, reverb, dist and chorus
notes: All ten combinations behave exactly as before: delay, dist and chorus stay at peak 0.0000 with one distinct value, tapetwo raises a null function pointer and reverb keeps calling outside its window. Using one consistent state object is not what they need

hypothesis: The silent effects are waiting on a host allocator, so returning pointers instead of zero unblocks them
test: Add a bump allocator to opzsim's host-call path (a fresh address per call, stepping by 0x10000 inside the machine window) and run init then renderFX for delay, tapetwo, reverb, dist and chorus
notes: Identical to returning zero in every case: delay, dist and chorus stay at peak 0.0000 with one distinct value, tapetwo still raises a null function pointer and reverb still keeps calling outside its window. The missing piece is not an allocation the harness can answer

hypothesis: The engines bundled in the decrypted firmware (1.2.45) are different builds that might behave better
test: Recover from-sergey/opz-1.2.45-decrypted.zip by walking its local file headers (the central directory is missing), extract the 13 engines under system/content/engines/, compare hashes with engines-official and re-run the instrument and effect tests
notes: 11 of the 13 are indeed different builds (only ep and organ are byte-identical), but behaviour is essentially unchanged: of the instruments only ep plays, the same as before, and of the effects chorus2 and crush behave as the official builds do (crush is actually silent in this build) while delay, dist, chorus, fdnreverb and reverb still fail. The blocker is therefore structural rather than specific to one firmware version

hypothesis: Stubbing the unmapped 0x04xxxxxx region with zeros lets the boot finish and populate the plug registry
test: Map 0x04000000 as zero pages, step the reset vector ignoring opzos' segment-coverage stop, and continue past RTS returns for 3,000,000 steps
notes: The boot runs 3,000,000 steps and ends at 0x0457fa56 - beyond the 1 MB stub, i.e. it walks off into unmapped space executing zeros - and the plug registry at 0x81059280 is still 0x0. Stubbing the missing region does not let the firmware initialise

hypothesis: digital's 659 Hz miss is only a too-short analysis window
test: Render note 76 at 0.4/0.8/1.2/1.6 s with three parameter levels, then repeat the six-pitch check at 1.2 s
notes: At 1.2 s the miss appeared to clear (8.2e4 vs 6.8e4) but an identical repeat minutes later failed (7.7e4 vs 8.5e4), so the result is not reproducible run to run. The claim therefore stays at the conservative 5 of 6: digital's 659 Hz behaviour is unstable rather than merely mis-measured

hypothesis: digital really only plays 5 of 6 pitches
test: Test the six pitches at EXACTLY 440*2^((note-69)/12) rather than rounded values (659.255 rather than 659.3), with 1.2 s renders, then compare with the rounded run
notes: At exact frequencies digital plays all 6 of 6. The apparent miss at note 76 came from evaluating the DFT 0.045 Hz off the true tone, which is under one DFT bin but enough to swing the magnitude by 20 percent. chord reads 1 of 6 and ep 2 of 6 under the same exact-frequency method

hypothesis: chord and ep were only being misjudged by an unfair neighbour test, as digital's 659 Hz was
test: Measure the contrast of the fundamental against the broadband floor (mag(f0) / median magnitude 200-2500 Hz) for six pitches per engine, an independent measure that does not compare against a fifth
notes: digital's fundamental stands 124 to 285 times above the floor at every pitch, while chord manages 1.8 to 14.8 and ep 3.3 to 21.6. The contrast measure corroborates the neighbour test: digital is solidly playing, chord and ep are not

hypothesis: chord uses the same pitch scale as digital (48000/32768)
test: Sweep chord's pitch argument against a 440 Hz target using the contrast metric with 200 blocks, find the best argument, then test four targets at that scale
notes: chord's contrast peaks at an argument of 150, not 300, i.e. a table period of 16384 bytes rather than 32768. At that scale it plays all four targets (contrast 18-44 while its fifth stays 2-7), and through the app path it now passes 6 of 6 pitches with contrast 17-31. digital remains 6 of 6 at 32768; ep is insensitive to the argument at every scale

hypothesis: The remaining instruments also have their own table period, findable by the same sweep that fixed chord
test: Sweep the pitch argument (75-600) against a 440 Hz target for ep, electric, volt, cluster, organ, sampleplayergain and synthsampler, measuring fundamental contrast, then refine any candidate
notes: None reaches a working contrast: ep 2.5, electric 9.7, volt 1.5, cluster 1.0, organ 2.2, and sampleplayergain and synthsampler are silent. Refining electric against a 220 Hz target gives an identical contrast of 38.9 at every argument from 19 to 112, i.e. it ignores the pitch argument entirely and produces a fixed spectrum. Only digital (32768) and chord (16384) calibrate

hypothesis: A parameter acts as a mix level gating the silent effects (dist, chorus, delay) on
test: Set all eight params to 0x00000000, 0x08000000, 0x20000000, 0x40000000 and 0x7fffffff and render each effect
notes: No value produces output: dist, chorus and delay stay at peak 0.0000 across all five settings and reverb raises its usual error, so a gating parameter is not what silences them

hypothesis: crush can be verified correct by its factory preset producing quantisation
test: Run crush with the parameter values from its factory preset and count outputs whose low 16 bits are zero
notes: 191 distinct outputs from the preset, but only 2 of 192 have zero low bits and just 1 of 192 is identical to its input, so crush transforms the signal without exhibiting the plain bit reduction its name suggests. Its correctness remains unestablishable without a reference

hypothesis: ep passes the two-note test, so it partially plays
test: Sweep ep's pitch argument at a 220 Hz target and measure fundamental contrast at each value
notes: ep's contrast is 6.4 at every argument from 19 to 300, i.e. it ignores the pitch argument completely and produces a fixed spectrum. Its earlier two-note passes were coincidences of the neighbour test, which never checked that changing the note changes the output

hypothesis: chord's 6-of-6 contrast result means it passes a strict note-dependence test
test: Add a pitch-dependence requirement to opzfactorycheck (the tone at note A must be at least 1.5x stronger in note A's render than in note B's) and re-run
notes: chord gives 3.3e5 at 220 Hz when 220 is requested against 2.6e5 when 440 is requested - only 1.27x - because it emits strong fixed partials alongside the tracked fundamental. digital passes the strict test cleanly (5.0e5 vs 3.2e5 at 220 and its 440 energy is note-specific). So under the strictest criterion only digital is verified, with chord strongly suggestive by contrast (17-31x at all six pitches, fifth 2-7x)

hypothesis: chord fails the note-dependence test, so it does not track pitch
test: Replace the raw-energy dependence test with a contrast-based one (how far the tone stands above the broadband floor, which is what isolates tracking from fixed partials) and re-run
notes: In contrast terms chord's 220 Hz tone stands 23.8x above the floor when 220 is requested and 9.5x when 440 is, a ratio of 2.51 - it does track, on top of fixed partials. digital is 643x and ep exactly 1.00, so the contrast measure separates the three correctly where raw energy did not

hypothesis: The two working engines only play through the internal harness, not the app itself
test: Request /api/render from the running opzenginetool for digital and chord at notes 57 and 69, decode the served WAV and measure the fundamental's contrast against the band floor
notes: Both play through the app's own HTTP interface: digital gives contrast 179 at 220 Hz and 248.6 at 440 Hz with peak 0.124, chord 23.8 and 28.2 with peak 0.068. So the two verified engines are working end to end - engine, app path, served audio - not only in the test harness

hypothesis: The four erroring instruments were only judged by crashing, so sweeping their voice gain might reveal one that plays
test: Render analoga, fm003b, ministringshort and saw013a at voice gains 0x08000000, 0x10000000, 0x20000000, 0x40000000 and 0x7fffffff, measuring fundamental contrast
notes: All twenty combinations raise the same error at the same place - 'engine keeps calling outside its window' - so the gain has no influence and these four are blocked before they produce a sample, not misjudged by the test

hypothesis: sampleplayergain only needs a valid note-to-sample descriptor index in params[0] >> 0x17
test: Supply 4096 samples of synthetic 440 Hz PCM at state+0xc with its length at state+0x8, then sweep the descriptor index over 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 48 and 64
notes: Every descriptor value renders peak 0.0000, so the selector is not the only missing input - the sample engines need the descriptor table and the sample-loading contract as well, neither of which an unbooted image supplies

hypothesis: ep takes its pitch from a state slot other than the argument, so seeding the right slot would make it track
test: Seed ctx+0x00 to ctx+0x2c in steps of 4 with the Q16 pitch and measure the fundamental's contrast at 220 Hz
notes: The baseline contrast is 6.1 and seeding every slot leaves it at 6.1 except ctx+0x04 (6.5) and ctx+0x08 (7.5), both far below the 10x that digital and chord reach; seeding ctx+0x30 makes the call fail to return. ep is pitch-insensitive regardless of where the value is placed

hypothesis: The pitch-insensitive engines take their note from onNoteOn rather than the render argument
test: Call onNoteOn with notes 57, 69 and 76 while rendering that note's frequency, measuring contrast at it, for ep, electric and cluster
notes: No engine tracks: ep gives 6.1, 2.4 and 3.9 at the three notes (all far below the 17-31 chord reaches), while electric and cluster stay at 0.0 at every note. The note handed to onNoteOn is not their pitch input either

hypothesis: The silent effects (dist, chorus, delay) use a different stack convention
test: Render each effect with two, five and six stack words, comparing peak output
notes: All three stay at peak 0.0000 under every convention while crush produces 0.019 only with the five-word form (0.000 with two or six words) - so five words is confirmed as the effects' convention and the three silent effects fail for a reason other than their arguments

hypothesis: delay's init takes its buffer, length, input and output as four stack words, and with that ordering it works
test: Try six orderings of (buffer, length, in, out) as init's stack arguments, then feed an impulse and a continuous sine to the delay that produced output
notes: The ordering (buf, len, in, out) does produce output - peak 0.9022 with 12 distinct values, where the other five orderings give 1 distinct value - but it is not a delay: an impulse produces nothing at all and a continuous sine yields a burst in the first two blocks followed by silence. It is a transient, not processed audio

hypothesis: The device's user preset file carries parameter values that would make engines play, unlike the factory one
test: Compare the two content-disk-dumps userPresets.dat files against from-sergey's plugPresets.dat by md5, noting that all three are 351,202 bytes
notes: The two user dumps are identical to each other (f6bcbba8...) and differ from the factory file (c587f37a...), so user-edited preset data does exist - but it is the same fixed-size format and the factory values were already shown to leave digital's output byte-identical, so different parameter values are not what the engines are missing

hypothesis: The pitch-insensitive engines read pitch from the bend argument rather than the pitch argument
test: Render ep, electric and cluster with bend set to 0, 0x10000, 0x1000000 and 0x10000000 and compare the dominant spectral peak
notes: The peak is identical at every bend value - 105.5 Hz for ep and electric and 750 Hz (the block rate) for cluster - so bend carries no pitch either. Every render argument, all eight params, twelve state slots and onNoteOn's note are now excluded as their pitch input

hypothesis: The pitch-insensitive instruments expect the six stack words in a different order
test: Render ep and electric with the current order (out, pitch, bend, ctx, params, amp) and four permutations of it, measuring fundamental contrast
notes: Only the current order produces output (ep 6.1, electric 37.4); every permutation gives 0.0. The instrument ABI is confirmed and neither engine tracks the note under any ordering

hypothesis: electric tracks the note when state+0x10..0x1c is seeded with the pitch, since its peak differed between 220 and 440 requests
test: Seed those four state words with the Q16 pitch and render 220 Hz and 440 Hz, comparing contrast at both frequencies for each request
notes: Both requests give identical spectra - contrast 50.6 at 220 Hz and 12.7 at 440 Hz - so electric emits a fixed tone containing 220 Hz whatever is asked for. The earlier differing peaks (0.0105 vs 0.0155) reflected different amounts of that same fixed content, not tracking

hypothesis: digital and chord play every pitch across the full MIDI range
test: Measure fundamental contrast at notes 36 to 96 in steps of 5 (65 Hz to 2093 Hz) for both engines
notes: digital passes 10 of 13 (failing 86, 91 and 96, i.e. 1174, 1397 and 1661 Hz) and chord 9 of 13 (failing 81 upward, 880 Hz and above). Both track cleanly from C2 to about C6 and degrade in the top register, so the earlier six-pitch sample overstated the range

hypothesis: The top register fails because the table period differs per band there
test: Render digital and chord at 1174 Hz (note 86) with periods 8192, 12288, 16384, 24576, 32768, 49152 and 65536
notes: No period works: digital peaks at contrast 9.0 (period 24576) and is 2.6-8.2 elsewhere, all below the 10x that working pitches reach, and chord is 1.1-2.4 at every value. The high-register degradation is not a period mismatch

hypothesis: The working engines are playing the high notes but decaying quickly, so an early window would show the tone
test: Compare tone-to-floor at an early window (0.083 s) against the tail for notes 61, 81, 86 and 91, then locate each note's dominant peak
notes: Early and late ratios match (digital 56.9 against 55.3 at 880 Hz), so decay is not the cause. The dominant peak above 880 Hz is the 750 Hz block rate for digital and 5-6 kHz content for chord, i.e. neither engine produces the requested tone in the top register at all

hypothesis: The top register is unreachable for digital because the pitch argument must stay inside the band table
test: Sweep the pitch argument from 200 to 1600 Hz while measuring contrast at 1174.7 Hz
notes: The note IS reachable: argument 900 gives contrast 19.1 at 1174.7 Hz, well above the 10x threshold, even though it lies past the band table's ~777 Hz top edge and past the linear prediction of 802. So the mapping becomes non-linear above the edge rather than failing, and the top register needs a different calibration rather than being impossible

hypothesis: A per-register calibration table can be fitted for the top register
test: For targets 1174.7 and 1396.9 Hz sweep the pitch argument across 700-1500 Hz and take the best contrast at each target, repeating 1174.7 across runs
notes: The best argument for 1174.7 Hz is 900 in one run and 1300 in the next, and 1396.9 Hz never exceeds contrast 4.3 at any argument. The contrast metric itself is unstable at these frequencies, so no reliable per-register mapping can be fitted from it - the top register is measurement-limited rather than merely uncalibrated

hypothesis: The high-register measurements are unstable, so no mapping can be fitted
test: Re-render the same arguments twice and compare samples, then measure the contrast at each candidate argument and at the linear prediction for each, all in one run
notes: Renders are byte-identical on repeat, and the measurements reproduce: arg 900 gives 19.1 and arg 1300 gives 26.5 at 1174.7 Hz. I had mis-read two runs that simply had different candidate sets. What is real is folding: arg 600 puts its tone at 879 Hz (the linear 1.4648x) but arg 1900 puts it at 1397 Hz, exactly half of its 2783 Hz prediction, and arg 1300 at 1175 rather than 1904 - so above the band edge the output folds instead of tracking linearly

hypothesis: The block-rate component can be removed by detrending each block, revealing the tone as the dominant peak
test: Subtract each 64-frame block's least-squares offset and slope, then take the dominant peak for arguments 300, 600, 900, 1300 and 1900
notes: The dominant peak stays at exactly 750 Hz (48 kHz / 64) with contrast 491-703 for every argument, so the artefact is not a per-block linear ramp. Throughout these engines' output a block-rate component dominates at roughly 500-1500x the musical tone (which measures 20-70 by contrast), which is why plain peak-picking has misled every measurement and why only targeted contrast at a known frequency reads the note

hypothesis: The block-rate artefact exists because a state field sets the block length and we leave it wrong
test: For each ctx offset 0x00-0x3c set values 8, 16 and 32 and count stores into the output buffer during one render call, comparing against the untouched baseline
notes: No field changes the count: every render writes exactly 130 stores into the output region, so the block length is fixed at 64 in the engines' own code and no input can alter it. The 750 Hz component is therefore inherent to the engine-host interface as we drive it, not a mis-set parameter

hypothesis: Each block is a delta the host should accumulate, which would remove the block-rate artefact
test: Render 140 blocks, then compare the spectrum as-is, after cumulative summation and after differencing, at arguments 300 and 600 with an 8192-sample window
notes: Accumulation amplifies the artefact rather than removing it (dominant 375 Hz at contrast 5132 against 489 as-is) and differencing destroys the tone (target contrast 1.4). Neither accumulation, differencing, per-block mean removal nor per-block linear detrending removes the block-rate component

hypothesis: The engines write audio, and the block-rate artefact is a secondary component
test: Dump the first and last sample, mean and peak of each of 16 consecutive blocks for digital at argument 300
notes: Each block is a monotone ramp that restarts at the block boundary (block 0 runs -1,228,178 to 88,617,972; block 7 runs 141,060,485 to 113,265,362) and blocks 2 and 3 are nearly silent (mean 8,001 and 22,588). The output is not a waveform at all: the musical information sits in each block's slope, and the block-rate artefact is the ramp restart, which is why no host transform recovers a clean note

hypothesis: Differencing within each block isolates the slope and so reveals the note
test: Take within-block first differences (resetting at each 64-sample boundary), optionally re-accumulate, and measure the dominant peak and target contrast at arguments 300 and 600
notes: Within-block differencing is worse than reading the output as-is: target contrast falls from 119.1 to 3.0 at 440 Hz and from 30.7 to 0.5 at 879 Hz. The tone is therefore already present and strong in the raw output (119x contrast against the band floor); the artefact is an additive component sitting above it, not a mis-interpretation of ramps

hypothesis: The two working engines only hold up at the two notes previously checked through the app
test: Request /api/render for notes 45, 52, 57, 64, 69, 72, 76 and 81 from the running tool and measure the fundamental's contrast in the served WAV
notes: Both hold up across the range: digital gives contrast 128-309 at notes 45-76 and 44.8 at 81 (8 of 8 above 10x), and chord 21.5-36.7 at 45-76 and 1.4 at 81 (7 of 8). Verified end to end through the app's own HTTP interface, not just the internal harness

hypothesis: The silent engines write to a different offset in the output region and we read the wrong place
test: Hook every store during one render and count nonzero writes across out-2048 to out+4096 for organ, sampleplayergain, synthsampler and cluster
notes: organ, sampleplayergain and synthsampler write nothing anywhere in that window, so they genuinely produce no output rather than writing elsewhere; cluster writes 29 nonzero offsets between +16 and +316, which matches the sparse fixed spectrum it was already known to emit

hypothesis: The effect call convention is five stack words, as opzenginesweep assumes
test: Decompile the OS FX manager: CallersOf on the FxManager.cpp string (0x8156f22c) gives FUN_8012ced0 and FUN_8012d024, whose code shows (*puVar4[2])(param_4, param_5, state, param_6), then test four-argument orders on all eight effects
notes: renderFX is called with FOUR arguments in the firmware - (param_4, param_5, state, param_6) where param_4/param_5 come from the voice dispatcher FUN_80117f4c - and init receives five, its fourth being a params pointer computed from the table at 0x8156f21c. Testing the four-argument form, chorus2 responds to (out, in, state, X) with peak 0.785 while the other seven stay silent; the five-word stack used so far is not what the OS does

hypothesis: The params table the firmware passes to init (0x8156f21c indexing 0x8112b21c) holds static per-slot values we can read and supply
test: Read both addresses out of opz.ldr's segment payloads
notes: Neither address is in any segment payload: 0x8156f21c is absent and 0x8112b21c reads as four zero bytes from a zerofill segment, so both are BSS filled at runtime by the FX manager. The per-slot parameter pointers therefore cannot be recovered from the image and have to be constructed by the running OS - the same wall as everywhere else

hypothesis: The buffer at 0x8112b21c holds a readable per-effect parameter layout we can synthesise
test: List its references and decompile FUN_80033cf8, which reads it at several offsets
notes: The readers are not FX parameter handlers: FUN_80033cf8 converts sample formats using fields at param_1+0x16/+0x22/+0x28, and a second reader sits in L2 code at 0x08039508 in the audio path. The FX manager's pointer is '&DAT_8112b21c + table[slot-8]', i.e. different slots are handed different offsets into a shared runtime audio/param region rather than a documented per-effect block, so there is no static layout to synthesise

hypothesis: Calling init and renderFX exactly as the firmware does makes the effects process audio
test: Call init(state, slot, 0, params_ptr, 0x8156f2b8) and renderFX(out, in, state, ctx) - the exact forms read from FUN_8012ced0 - for all eight effects
notes: Only chorus2 emits anything, and only 6 nonzero samples out of 384 - a transient rather than processed audio. chorus, crush, delay and dist write nothing, fdnreverb and tapetwo raise a null function pointer and reverb keeps calling outside its window. Reproducing the firmware's own calling convention exactly is therefore not sufficient either

hypothesis: The 230 MB APK embeds a firmware image containing the missing 0x04xxxxxx region
test: List every file over 2 MB and every entry matching zfw/firmware/.bin/.ldr in OP-Z_1.3.0_APKPure.apk
notes: There are no firmware entries at all: the large files are Unity runtime libraries (libil2cpp.so 25.8 MB, libunity.so 23.7 MB), global-metadata.dat, the photomatic video and three videopak rooms. The APK carries only the app and its factory plug metadata, no OS image
